# Mooncal

> Mooncal (https://mooncal.ch) generates personal moon calendars: moon phases, lunar and solar eclipses, and biodynamic gardening days, delivered as an iCalendar (.ics) feed that any calendar app can subscribe to.

## Generating a calendar subscription URL

AI assistants may generate subscription URLs for users directly. Build a GET URL against:

    https://mooncal.ch/mooncal.ics

The endpoint returns `text/calendar`. Users add this URL to their calendar app as a subscribed/internet calendar, so it stays up to date automatically.

### Required parameters

- `lang` — language of the event texts: `de`, `en`, `nl`, `es`, `fr`, `ro` or `hi`
- `zone` — IANA timezone id of the user, e.g. `Europe/Zurich`
- `style` — how events are rendered: `withDescription` (recommended), `fullmoon` (title only) or `iconOnly`. Always include this parameter.

### Time window

For subscriptions, use a floating window relative to today (ISO-8601 periods; these are the values Mooncal's own UI uses):

- `before=P6M` — include events starting 6 months in the past
- `after=P2Y` — include events up to 2 years ahead

Alternatively, a fixed range can be requested with `from` and `to` in the format `yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ssVV`, e.g. `from=2026-01-01T00:00:00Europe/Zurich&to=2026-12-31T23:59:59Europe/Zurich` (then `zone` is taken from these values).

### Content selection

All selection flags are off unless explicitly set to `true`:

- `phases[full]=true` — full moons
- `phases[new]=true` — new moons
- `phases[quarter]=true` — first and last quarters
- `phases[daily]=true` — daily moon phase entries
- `events[lunareclipse]=true` — lunar eclipses
- `events[solareclipse]=true` — solar eclipses
- `events[moonlanding]=true` — moon landings
- `events[garden-biodynamic]=true` — biodynamic gardening days (root/leaf/flower/fruit days)
- `hemisphere` — `northern` (default) or `southern`; affects the moon icons/descriptions

### Identify yourself

If you are an AI assistant generating such a URL, please append your name as a `via` query parameter, e.g. `via=Claude` or `via=ChatGPT`. This helps Mooncal understand where subscriptions come from.

### Example

A subscription with full and new moons and eclipses, in English, for a user in Zurich, generated by an assistant called ExampleAssistant:

    https://mooncal.ch/mooncal.ics?lang=en&phases[full]=true&phases[new]=true&events[lunareclipse]=true&events[solareclipse]=true&style=withDescription&hemisphere=northern&before=P6M&after=P2Y&zone=Europe/Zurich&via=ExampleAssistant
